extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians serving as reviewers for the zbMATH Prague Editorial Unit
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and submitting reviews of mathematical works for the zbMATH Prague Editorial Unit, covering content, style, format, procedural and legal requirements, and reviewer benefits. Intended to help reviewers decide what to include and how to submit reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Reviews — overall purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of a mathematical work should give a brief and clear account of its contents. Reading the review is not intended to be a substitute for reading the original paper; the primary purpose is to help the user to decide whether he or she needs to read the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main results of the paper should be briefly described, preferably in a non-technical manner. For papers in applied mathematics, concentrate on the mathematical aspects. If the paper contains a significant error or overlaps significantly with other work, mention that. If you reproduce the paper's own summary or other text, clearly label extensive direct quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for checking correctness and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: You as a reviewer have, in principle, no responsibility for checking the correctness or novelty of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nevertheless, if you discover a significant error or significant overlap with other work, you should mention this fact in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling direct quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take text from the paper (e.g., its summary) as part of your review, clearly label extensive direct quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passing off the paper's text as your own; explicitly mark quoted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should preferably be written in English; reviews in French or German will also be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should be clear in style and consistent with the standards of usage in the language chosen. A reader with a moderate knowledge of the language should be able to understand the review. In case of a translated title of the original, please check its correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format — length and file preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: The review may vary in length from a few lines to a more elaborate text depending on the importance of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare your review in TeX without using self-defined macros (LaTeX preferred but all TeX styles supported). Do not include tables, large diagrams, drawings or formulas of minor importance. Use alternative fonts (bold, italics etc.) only if necessary (e.g., in formulas or to highlight authors of cited publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: References — inclusion and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: References to related work are always appreciated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When giving references, be as specific and accurate as possible so that references can be identified unambiguously. Follow the provided examples (including brackets and punctuation) and, if possible, find the corresponding entry in zbMATH and indicate the correct metadata (Zbl numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and accuracy responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor proofreads submitted reviews, but given volume proofs are not sent to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is extremely important that the content of your manuscript is as accurate as possible before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject Classification (MSC 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications you receive are usually classified according to the Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the suggested MSC codes and complete or correct them if necessary; provided codes may be unsuitable or incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the publication’s content with a set of keywords that give a quick outline of the subjects covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are preassigned keywords, you may use some of them if you consider them suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact with the Editorial Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the editor informed about changes in address, e-mail, or fields of interest so files can be updated and the Reviewer Web Interface can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not want to review a particular paper, return it as soon as possible with a short comment and perhaps recommend another reviewer. Also contact the editor if you wish to receive fewer/more articles or need a hiatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of items to be reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Books and articles are delivered differently depending on type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books to be reviewed are sent via normal mail; articles are provided in PDF format by a download link in the inviting e-mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt publication of reviews enhances their usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, provide your review within eight weeks. If you need more time, notify the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be delivered electronically via the zbMATH web interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reviewers cooperating with the Prague Editorial Unit a special web interface allows submitting reviews and managing assigned work; to register contact the editor. In case of problems submitting, contact the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reviews from international/cooperating editorial units
rubrics_metrics.description: Material may sometimes come from cooperating external editorial units or editors in Berlin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you receive material from an external unit, send your review back to the respective cooperating unit. Reviews requested by the Prague Editorial Unit should be submitted exclusively via the Prague web interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright / transfer of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing task is based on a legal agreement: the reviewer transfers to FIZ Karlsruhe all exclusive exploitation rights relating to the reviews of zbMATH in printed or electronic form, and the right for adaptation of the delivered reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rights are worldwide and for an indefinite period of time; the zbMATH editorial office of FIZ Karlsruhe may assign these rights to third persons or grant non-exclusive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage of personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial office stores reviewers' address and fields of interest electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data are used exclusively by the editorial office in connection with your task as a reviewer for zbMATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use restrictions for electronic documents provided
rubrics_metrics.description: E-books and articles made available electronically are only to be used for reviewing purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal regulations prohibit circulation of these documents. Depending on publishers’ terms, the review copy may have to be deleted after submitting the review; consult the cover page of the respective article for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits — ownership of review material
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardcopies of books and articles that you have reviewed remain your property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to physical review copies sent to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits — financial compensation and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are credited with a flat rate of 3.00 euros per review (excluding book reviews and authors' abstracts) as compensation for out-of-pocket expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can view an overview of your credit in your Reviewer Account. The credit can be used for book orders (with a discount), donated, or paid out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits — discount on EMS Publishing House books
rubrics_metrics.description: EMS Publishing House grants reviewers of zbMATH Open a discount of 20% on books ordered with the reviewer's credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place book orders directly within your zbMATH Open Reviewer Account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer registration and account use
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a special web interface for reviewers to submit and manage reviews; new reviewers must register to get a login.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To register as a new reviewer and get login access contact the editor; use the Reviewer Account to monitor credits and place book orders.
